title: Demons as the spirits of dead Nephilim giants

tellings.quote: Demons according to ancient Hebrew cosmology are the disembodied spirits of dead giants that persist in the world.
Remember I said in the book of Enoch that when this when the giants were killed that their spirits departed their bodies
tellings.difference: Credits the Book of Enoch specifically, where the story's telling says 'ancient Hebrew cosmology', and describes the spirits leaving the giants' bodies when they were killed.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the claim that the spirits of the dead giants became demons; the teller is the same.

as_told.title: Book of Enoch: spirits of dead giants become demons

tellings.quote: And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.

Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from =men=, 〚and〛 from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; ⌜they shall be evil spirits on earth, and⌝ evil spirits shall they be called.

And the spirits of the giants =afflict=, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, ⌜but nevertheless hunger⌝ and thirst, and cause offences.

From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death ⌜of the giants⌝, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great ⌜judgement⌝ in which the age shall be consummated over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated.”

plain: The idea is that demons are the ghosts of the Nephilim, the giants that ancient Jewish writings say were born when fallen angels called the Watchers mated with human women, and that when the giants were killed their spirits left their bodies and stayed on Earth. A researcher of giant lore named Tim Alberino tells Michels this, first calling it "ancient Hebrew cosmology" and then pointing to the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text outside the standard Bible, in the 1917 English translation by R. H. Charles. The text he names lines up closely with what he says. It says the giants, "produced from the spirits and flesh," shall be called "evil spirits upon the earth," that "evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies," and that their beginning is "from the holy Watchers." It says these spirits "afflict, oppress, destroy" and "take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst," and that from "the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants" their spirits go forth to destroy until the final judgement. The book calls them evil spirits rather than demons, but what it describes, spirits of dead giants left roaming the earth to do harm, is the same thing Alberino means. For him it would explain where demons come from.
